claims.claim: The tool installs nothing: it runs on the Python standard library alone.
claims.method: the package imports only json, argparse, subprocess, pathlib, re, time; pyproject declares an empty dependency list

claims.claim: The CLI exposes run, check and list.
The version the package reports equals the version in pyproject.toml.

cmd: python3 -c "import tomllib,pathlib; print('manifest', tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['version'])" 2>/dev/null || python3 -c "import re,pathlib; print('manifest', re.search(r'^version = \"([^\"]+)\"', pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(), re.M).group(1))"

claims.claim: The example repository's claims all reproduce.
claims.metric: counts printed by a run over example/
claims.method: the example reads example/data.json and prints its numbers; the claims file asserts that output

claims.claim: Strict mode turns a manual (unchecked) claim into a failed run.
claims.method: the example carries one claim that no command can check; --strict must reject it
claims.repro: python3 -m verify_claims --root example run --strict; echo exit=$?

check.cmd: python3 -m verify_claims --root example run --strict >/dev/null 2>&1; echo exit=$?

claims.claim: A claim with neither a command nor a written reason is refused, and the tool refuses to run such a file.
claims.method: tests/fixtures/invalid/claims.json omits the check block on purpose
claims.repro: python3 -m verify_claims --root tests/fixtures/invalid check; python3 -m verify_claims --root tests/fixtures/invalid run; echo exit=$?

check.cmd: python3 -m verify_claims --root tests/fixtures/invalid run >/dev/null 2>&1; echo exit=$?

claims.metric: tests reported by the standard-library runner

check.cmd: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | grep -o '^Ran [0-9]* tests'

claims.claim: docs/case-studies.md documents six failure modes (plus the section on wrongly written checks).
claims.method: the document groups the audited failures by mode; this claim keeps the count honest
